title: Release Gate Communication Playbook for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Capture a concrete, repeatable playbook for scope lock, cut criteria, milestone cadence, and release notes coordination across API, Console, and Runtime teams. This ticket centralizes owners, timelines, gating metrics, and GTM artifacts so that engineering, design, docs, support, and GTM teams can execute a coordinated launch with a clear rollback/mitigation plan.

Summary of approach:
1) Milestone cadence: define two hard milestones (Feature Freeze, Cut/Ship) with a single soft milestone (Code Complete) in between. Feature Freeze = no new customer-facing features merged without documented exception. Code Complete = all planned merges are in main and all integration tests pass. Cut/Ship = final artifacts signed off and release branch created.
2) Scope lock and exceptions: scope lock occurs at Feature Freeze. Exceptions must be routed through a triage committee (PM, Eng Tech Lead, SRE, Design) and require documented risks and mitigation steps.
3) Cut criteria (final checklist): automated test pass rate >= 98% on main CI, end-to-end smoke tests pass in staging, performance SLOs validated on representative load (p50/p95 under target), no outstanding P0/P1 bugs, release notes draft approved, documentation pages in docs repo updated, canary plan defined.
4) Release notes coordination: designate a primary release-notes owner (PM) and secondary owners per surface (API, Console, Runtime). Owners collect PR summaries, user-visible changes, migration notes, and breaking-change warnings. Use the release notes template and fill sections: Overview, User Impact, Migration Steps, Deprecations, API Contract Changes, Known Issues, Rollout Plan.
5) Cross-team GTM tasks: compile a short-run GTM checklist for marketing, developer relations, sales enablement, and support — includes comms schedule, one-pager, demo recording, sandbox refresh, and runtime cost guidance.
6) Communication windows: align weekly triage syncs during the run-up, daily standup during the final 72 hours, and a 1-hour cross-functional ship call at T-2 hours. Publish status updates to #release-ops and a one-line summary to #all-engineering and the product mailing list at each milestone.

Why this differs from existing artifacts: This playbook focuses on communication templates, concrete gating metrics, and a cross-surface owner matrix instead of only milestone dates. It codifies exception handling and release note formatting expectations so downstream teams can reliably produce GTM artifacts without last-minute rework.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: Feature Freeze date and exception process communicated to all teams and logged in runbook
AC2: Release notes draft exists with sections completed for API/Console/Runtime and assigned owners
AC3: Cut criteria checklist is executable and referenced by release branch checklist
AC4: GTM checklist items assigned and scheduled (marketing, devrel, sales, support)
AC5: Canary plan with clear pass/fail thresholds and rollback steps documented
tasks: Create release branch and tag (ENG) — owner: Release Engineer
Run performance validation harness against staging (SRE/ENG) — owner: SRE Lead
Produce release notes draft and confirm user-visible changes (PM/Docs) — owner: Priya Rao
Update Console screenshots and help text (Design) — owner: Design Lead
Prepare GTM one-pager and demo build (Marketing/DevRel) — owner: Marketing Lead
Confirm legal/compliance sign-off for customer communications (Legal) — owner: Legal Ops
rollout_checklist: Canary deployment in us-west-2 with 5% traffic for 6 hours
Monitor error budget burn rate and latency p95 during canary
Increment traffic to 25% for 3 hours if stable
Full traffic cutover after 24 hours of stable metrics
Update customer-facing status page with scheduled window and post-mortem link
rollback_steps: Step 1: Abort cut and freeze traffic ramp at current percentage
Step 2: Re-route traffic to previous compatible runtime/model variant using smart routing policy
Step 3: Revert release branch or deploy hotfix to address regression
Step 4: Run focused regression tests on staging and small canary before retry
Step 5: Post-incident review and update runbook with lessons learned
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Last-minute API contract change breaks SDK consumers — Mitigation: require API compatibility sign-off and run contract tests against SDKs
Risk: Performance regression under long-context workloads — Mitigation: run 12-hour longer-duration soak tests and hold ship if p95 exceeds threshold
Risk: Docs and release notes mismatch — Mitigation: lock docs PRs 24 hours before ship and assign a docs triage lead
